newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba says German Q1 net borrowing stood at 33.9 bln dmk.
newsitem.headline: Buba says German Q1 net borrowing stood at 33.9 bln dmk.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday that net borrowing by German central, regional and local authorities in the first quarter of this year was nearly twice as high as the same period last year.

In its May report, the Bundesbank said the government's net borrowing stood at 33.9 billion marks compared with 17.8 billion marks a year ago. During the first two months of 1997, total net borrowing stood at 33.1 billion marks.
Buba says German Q1 net borrowing stood at 33.9 bln dmk

Bonn had set itself a net borrowing target of around 53.4 billion marks for the whole of 1997 but Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Wednesday said he might need to raise this target in light of stubbornly high unemployment levels.

Of the 33.9 billion mark total borrowed during first quarter, the federal government made up the lion's share, borrowing 33.5 billion marks. A year ago the federal government borrowed only 18.9 billion marks and it borrowed 30.8 billion marks in January and February.
The state governments or Laender borrowed some 2.5 billion marks during the first quarter 1997 while the local authorities borrowed 1.6 billion marks.
In January and February, the Laender borrowed 7.8 billion marks while the local authorities borrowed 1.6 billion marks.
The federal cash deficit climbed to 40.74 billion marks in the first four months of the year compared with 39.07 billion marks in January to March.
During April, however, the cash deficit declined to 1.68 billion from 7.27 billion marks in March. In April 1996 the monthly cash deficit stood at 2.75 billion marks.
The Bundesbank said the reason for the movement in April was that cash receipts rose 6.2 percent while the cash expenditures rose only 3.4 percent.
In March, cash receipts rose by 18.5 percent with expenditures rising by 20.9 percent.
A special factor during the month was that the federal government had received part of the Bundesbank's annual profits.
However, the Bundesbank also stressed that cash deficits often do not present a very accurate reflection of the budget.
